title: Emit kernel-selection + quant-mode tracing spans (shapes + per-op timers) behind flag
author: Yuki Sato
description:
Context: As part of the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint we need consistent attribution for (a) which kernel family was selected and why, and (b) where time is actually going during prefill vs decode for quantized paths. Today the benchmark harness can measure end-to-end phase timings, but when a run regresses it’s hard to tie the regression to kernel selection changes (auto-selector drift), unexpected fallback to FP16, or shape-dependent kernel behavior.

This PR adds low-overhead tracing spans and counters that make kernel selection and per-op timing visible in traces/log ingestion, guarded behind an explicit runtime flag so the default production overhead is ~0.

What’s included:
- New tracing spans around kernel selection and execution in the quantized attention + GEMM hot paths.
- Span attributes emitted (when enabled): model_family, quant_mode (fp8/int8/fp16), phase (prefill/decode), chosen_kernel (stable kernel_id + human readable family), and key shapes (batch_size, seq_len, hidden, num_heads, head_dim, m/n/k for GEMM where applicable).
- Optional per-op timing counters (nanosecond timers) attached as span events and exported via the existing runtime tracing pipeline. These are intended for benchmark runs and perf-canary; they are not enabled by default.
- Guardrails to avoid trace explosion: a) hard cap on emitted per-request op events, b) shape attribute bucketing for long-context runs (seq_len bucket + exact seq_len), and c) sampling hook for extremely high QPS runs.
- Logging of fallback reasons when auto-selector chooses a non-quant kernel (e.g., unsupported shape, alignment constraints, capability mismatch), attached to the kernel-selection span.

How to enable:
- Runtime config: runtime.tracing.quant_kernels_enabled=true
- Optional: runtime.tracing.quant_kernels_emit_op_events=true (adds per-op timer events; recommended only in perf lab / canary)
- Optional: runtime.tracing.quant_kernels_max_op_events_per_request (default 64)

Why tracing (vs logs only):
- Traces already carry request-scoped context (route/model/version, region, GPU SKU tags) and are what the benchmark ingestion pipeline and dashboard tooling expects. This makes it straightforward to join benchmark artifacts with runtime trace data for attribution without adding a parallel log parser.

Performance/overhead:
- When disabled: a single branch + no allocations on the hot path (span creation is a no-op). Verified via microbench (see notes below).
- When enabled: overhead depends on emit_op_events; kernel-selection span only is ~sub-microsecond per request on H100 in perf lab. emit_op_events adds measurable overhead and should be used only for targeted profiling/benchmark runs.

Testing:
- Added unit tests for: span attribute correctness (quant_mode, kernel_id), fallback reason emission, and shape bucketing behavior.
- Added a small integration test that runs a single request through INT8 and asserts spans are emitted when the flag is set.

Notes for benchmark sprint:
- This is a dependency for ENG-24814 and will be used by the benchmark harness owners to attribute anomalies (e.g., INT8 shape-specific auto-selector mismatch; FP8 prefill regression investigations). Follow-up PR will add benchmark artifact ingestion tags mapping to these span fields.

Rollout plan:
- Land behind default-off flags.
- Enable in perf-lab and quant perf-canary jobs first.
- If stable, optionally enable kernel-selection span (without per-op events) for a small internal hosted cohort during investigations (timeboxed).
commits: runtime/tracing: add QuantKernelTraceConfig feature flags + defaults
runtime/kernels: instrument kernel auto-selection span + fallback reasons
runtime/quant: add per-op timer events for quant GEMM/attention hot path
runtime/testing: add span attribute + bucketing unit tests
docs: runtime tracing flag documentation and perf-lab guidance
conversation:
Noah Patel (review): A bit worried about attribute cardinality here. Exact seq_len and m/n/k can explode. Can we bucket by default and only emit exact values behind a stricter flag? Also please confirm the default path is allocation-free.

Yuki Sato (author): Good call. Updated to always emit seq_len_bucket (e.g., 0-1k/1k-2k/2k-4k/4k-8k/8k+) and emit exact seq_len only when quant_kernels_emit_op_events=true. For GEMM shapes, emit m/n/k buckets plus exact only under emit_op_events. Verified via heap profiling: when flags are false, no allocations on the hot path (span creation is compile-time no-op in our wrapper).

Hiro Tanaka (review): For kernel_id: please make sure it’s stable across builds (string name is fine, but we need a stable enum/id for dashboards). Also include alignment constraints / capability checks in fallback reason.

Yuki Sato (author): Added stable kernel_id (uint32) from the registry + family string. Fallback reason now includes: unsupported_op, capability_mismatch, alignment, shape_not_supported, and forced_override. Included the first failing predicate for debuggability.

Allison Grant (review): Can you align attribute keys with the observability pack conventions? We use dot-separated keys and a prefix for runtime spans. Also please add a short section in docs about recommended usage (perf lab only) and caps.

Yuki Sato (author): Updated keys to runtime.quant.* (e.g., runtime.quant.mode, runtime.quant.kernel_id, runtime.quant.phase). Added docs section and emphasized max_op_events_per_request + sampling guidance.

Julian Moore (review): One more thing: phase labeling prefill/decode should match scheduler instrumentation naming; we’ve standardized on "prefill" and "decode" (not "prompt"/"gen").

Yuki Sato (author): Updated to prefill/decode throughout and added a unit test to prevent drift.

CI: initial run failed on lint due to new docs link formatting; fixed in 2b9d8d1.

Final approvals:
- Noah Patel: Approved
- Hiro Tanaka: Approved
- Allison Grant: Approved
- Julian Moore: Approved

Merged via squash to main.
release_notes: Runtime: Add optional tracing spans for quant kernel selection (FP8/INT8) including chosen kernel + bucketed shapes; default-off behind runtime.tracing.quant_kernels_enabled. Intended for perf lab / perf-canary attribution.
